Subject: Follow-up from today — dedicated vs hosted sizing

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying asks so your team can build the dedicated sizing proposal: 

- Current usage intent: customer-facing chat assistant (support + guided discovery) with some batch re-ranking for recommendations. Expected to go live to a subset of users in Q2.
- Traffic profile we discussed verbally: ~120 TPS at peak (burst up to 220 for a few minutes), average session ~3 completions.
- Latency goal: p95 generation <= 350ms for short responses (~100 tokens), p95 <= 700ms for longer responses (~600 tokens).
- Model preference: we are evaluating strong open models; leaning toward Llama2-70B 8-bit quant or similar. Open to guidance.

Can you confirm what GPU SKUs you recommend for that profile (we heard A100 vs H100 tradeoffs) and whether Dedicated or Private VPC would be the right next step? Also we can share sample traces if that helps — attaching a small token-shape CSV now.

Attachments: loopai_token_shape_sample.csv (CSV)

Thanks — Jordan

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-02-04T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — dedicated vs hosted sizing

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap, very helpful. Below is a short debrief and the specific inputs we need to size a Dedicated pool and compare it to Hosted/Private VPC.

Redwood recap / quick guidance:
- Deployment mode: Based on customer-facing, p95 targets, and peak bursts, Dedicated is likely the right fit for predictable throughput. Private VPC is recommended only if you need customer-managed network isolation or on-prem. Hosted can work for early stages but may be noisy for your p95 SLAs at 120–220 TPS.

Primary sizing questions (please confirm):
1) Peak sustained TPS window (minutes): you said bursts to 220 — how long do bursts last? Example: ~5 minutes, ~30 minutes?
2) Token mix: can you confirm average request tokens (prompt) and average response tokens (generation)? Your note mentioned ~100 short and ~600 long — proportion of each (e.g., 70% short, 30% long)?
3) Concurrency model: are requests single-turn (stateless) or do you expect large multi-turn sessions where KV cache reuse is high? This affects KV cache sizing and GPU memory choice.
4) Model: if you have a preferred model (Llama2-70B-8bit, Meta-closed alternatives, or smaller family), mention that — we can size quantized vs fp16 runs differently.
5) Batchability: can your app accept small batching (<=8) for short responses? If yes, we can recommend more cost-efficient pooling.

Preliminary SKU thoughts (subject to above):
- If bursts are short (<10m) and token mix skews short (>=70% 100-token responses): 4x A100 80GB (high throughput for many small requests with good NVLink memory) or 3x H100 80GB (better for very low-latency—H100 often better for recent attention optimizations).
- If many long generations (600 tokens) and multi-turn KV reuse: prefer H100 with 80GB and higher NVLink bandwidth to keep p95 lower.
- If you must minimize cost and accept higher p95 tail: consider a mix (reserved Dedicated pool + Hosted fallback) — we can draft a routing fallback plan.

Next steps I propose:
- You drop a 24–48h sample trace (real request timestamps + prompt/response token counts) to the Drive link (or attach) so we can run the sizing workbook.
- We'll fill the attached dedicated-sizing workbook and share a comparison: Dedicated SKU mix, estimated p95 latency, and monthly cost.
- Quick follow-up meeting: 30 minutes — propose Thu Feb 6 10:00 AM PT.

I've attached the sizing workbook and a short diagram showing Dedicated vs Private VPC tradeoffs.

Attachments: loopai-dedicated-sizing-workbook.xlsx; redwood-deploy-options-diagram.pdf

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Follow-up from today — dedicated vs hosted sizing

Marissa — looping you in. Jordan's numbers look like a mid-size Dedicated deal where procurement will want: commit tiers, lead time for HW reservation, and a clear fallback/overprovision plan.

Internal notes (do not forward externally):
- Need a quick estimate of committed vs burst capacity pricing (3/6/12 month options).
- Confirm realistic lead time for H100 reservations in our target region (us-west). If H100 lead times are 8+ weeks, propose an A100-first pathway with a migration plan.
- Ask infra to confirm whether we need extra NVMe scratch for long-generation workloads (their docs indicate ~50GB per model replica for caching).

Vivek — can you flag anything else for procurement to include in the quote? I will draft the pricing skeleton once we have the workbook filled.

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — dedicated vs hosted sizing

Thanks — quick answers inline and uploaded a 48h trace to the Drive folder you shared: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1LoopAI-Traces

- Burst length: typically 3–8 minutes, rare sustained over 15 minutes.
- Token mix: ~65% short (~120 tokens total), ~35% long (~550–700 tokens).
- Concurrency: sessions are multi-turn but KV reuse is low for the short-turn flows; re-ranking jobs are batched (usually batch size 16) and run off-peak.
- Model: initial POC will use Llama2-70B-8bit; we may test a trimmed 33B family for cost checks.
- Batchability: short-turn chat should not be batched more than 4 due to perceived latency. Re-ranking jobs are batchable 16–32 off-peak.

We accept the Dedicated recommendation. Please proceed with filling the workbook and include two SKU paths: (A) A100-first (fast availability), (B) H100-first (better p95 but potential lead time). Also include a hybrid routing plan (dedicated + hosted fallback).

Next meeting: Thu Feb 6 10:00 AM PT works for us. I will have our infra lead on the call.

Regards,
Jordan Price
Head of Platform, LoopAI
